html:
George Price was the leader who brought Belize to independence. He led the country from 1961 to 1984 and again from 1989 to 1993, and is called the Father of the Nation.

Born in Belize City, he trained for the priesthood before entering politics. In 1950 he helped found the People's United Party, which grew out of protests against the devaluation of the colony's currency. It demanded self-rule from Britain and resisted the claims of Guatemala.

British Honduras won self-government in 1964 with Price as premier. Independence was delayed by the Guatemalan claim and the fear of invasion, and came on 21 September 1981, with British troops staying on to guard the border. Price became the first prime minister of Belize. He also chose Belmopan as the new capital.
